name: acme-partner-access-path-nat
description: ILLUSTRATIVE Approach-3 example (DAG-sequenced program + inter-pipeline chaining) for firewall-policy-use-case.md — the SAME three-vendor partner-HTTPS path as Approach 2, with ONE change: edge-fw source-NATs the partner traffic to a pool it chooses at design time. Because the downstream hops must match that post-NAT source (which does not exist until the edge design runs), the legs are DAG-sequenced (edge -> dmz -> core) and the downstream legs chain the upstream leg's actual deliverable, instead of running in parallel against a static contract. NOT runnable as-is (no live PAN-OS / ASA / AWS harvest service; pan-os/cisco-asa protocols notional). Design worked-example, not a demo artifact.

sourceNat.toPool: RUNTIME — chosen by the edge-fw DESIGN from free addresses on its dmz-facing interface (harvested live); NOT a pre-agreed constant, which is exactly why it cannot live in the interface contract
sourceNat.consequence: dmz-sg and core-fw must match the POST-NAT source (the pool), not the partner CIDR

nodes.name: dmz-sg
nodes.matches: POST-NAT source pool (chained from edge-fw's deliverable), NOT 203.0.113.0/24

nodes.name: core-fw
nodes.matches: POST-NAT source pool (chained transitively from edge-fw via dmz), NOT 203.0.113.0/24

endToEndFlow.postNatSource: RUNTIME — the edge-fw NAT pool, produced by the edge design; downstream hops match THIS
endToEndFlow.notes: The ONLY delta from the Approach-2 topology is edge-fw's sourceNat. That one addition makes the source a downstream hop must match a RUNTIME value (chosen during the edge design, from live edge state) rather than a declarative constant — so this is Approach 3: DAG-sequenced (edge -> dmz -> core) with inter-pipeline chaining, not parallel + contract. Remove the NAT and it collapses back to Approach 2.

interdependency.mechanism: downstream leg dependencyIds include the upstream SIBLING pipeline id; the context-chainer PIPELINE-predecessor branch chains the upstream leg's report.md (the actual chosen pool) into the downstream leg's §6; the settledness predicate (F18) holds the downstream leg until the upstream deliverable is fully persisted, so a half-built NAT design is never chained forward
interdependency.whyNotContract: the pool is selected from addresses that are free on the edge's dmz-facing interface at design time (harvested live) — it is an OUTPUT of the edge design, not a value the Architect can agree up front. If it COULD be pre-agreed, you would fold it into the contract and run Approach 2 (parallel, proven).
